Brief A: planned HVAC replacement

Customer and scope: a homeowner considering a scheduled system replacement. The owner must define the equipment and work it actually accepts. The draft does not advertise emergency repair or dispatch.

Page plan: Home points to Replacement; the Replacement page explains accepted work and the assessment sequence; Process covers the visit and proposal; Coverage gives the true territory; About identifies the responsible business; Contact starts a review. Combine pages if the content does not justify six.

Proof to gather: approved installation photographs, accurate captions describing the business’s role, current credentials only if supported, and the actual assessment process. No efficiency saving, installation deadline or certification is invented.

Six intake fields: name, email, town/postal code, property type, current-system and project summary, preferred timing (optional). Do not ask for private access codes. A request is not an appointment or a technical recommendation.

Receipt and check: “Your replacement inquiry has been received for review. We will check the project and coverage before discussing an assessment.” Add only an owner-approved reply arrangement and real fallback contact. Test the saved request and recipient’s inbox.
Brief B: planned roof repair or replacement assessment

Customer and scope: a property owner asking whether an observed roofing issue fits accepted work. The contractor approves which materials, property types and jobs it handles. Do not imply emergency storm response or insurance-claim services without evidence.

Page plan: Home, Roofing Services, Assessment Process, approved Project Examples, Coverage and Contact. If repair and replacement need distinct explanations, adjust the list and scope before choosing a package.

Proof to gather: permissioned job photos, the work actually performed, supported material and service boundaries, and any verified qualification the owner elects to publish. A generic roof photograph is not evidence of a completed job.

Six intake fields: name, email, town/postal code, property type, issue or requested-work summary, preferred timing (optional). Ask for roof material only if known within the summary; do not encourage customers to climb for measurements or photos.
